solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Uncensored clip shot in Exodus

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters are placed inside the departure word

parts.note: an exodus is a mass departure, an exit

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters of clip are mixed up

explanation.surface: A filmed clip in the biblical epic Exodus shows something unsuitable for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' scrambles CLIP into PLIC, which goes 'in' EXIT (exodus). 'shot' looks like filming, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Explicit content shows sex or violence openly, with nothing cut by a censor.

clue.text: Bitterness, any time leader goes crazy

indicators.note: the first letter of 'any time' leaves
the remaining letters are thrown into a crazy order

parts.note: ANYTIME without its first letter A

explanation.surface: A grumble that people turn bitter whenever whoever is in charge loses the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Both the deletion and the scramble act on the same two words, in that order: drop the A, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Enmity is hostility, a bitter ill will between people.

clue.text: Get confused and balls up

definitions.note: read as a command, 'get (someone) confused', i.e. daze them

indicators.note: in a down entry, 'up' means the letters read from the bottom, turned round

parts.note: nuts is slang for testicles, balls

explanation.surface: Someone muddled makes a mess of things: gets confused and balls it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls up' looks like the British slang for making a mess of something; split apart, it is NUTS turned upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the causative sense: a stunning blow or surprise leaves someone dazed and unable to think straight.

clue.text: Stuff America — it possesses nothing attractive!

parts.note: to stuff yourself is to gorge
the United States
zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A sneer at America: stuff it, the place has nothing going for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' stands for America, the thing that possesses the O. The surface says America has nothing attractive; the wordplay makes it GORGEOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, pitched stronger: dazzling good looks are the top end of attractive.

clue.text: see 23dn.
Such fun for loony left to get in charge!

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so the letters of for are jumbled

explanation.surface: A jibe that the mad Left taking control would be a laugh, Private Eye style.
explanation.definitionFit: A frolic is a bout of lively play or merriment, so it is a kind of fun.

clue.text: Rod's bitter about kiss?

indicators.note: the beer goes about, around, the kiss

parts.note: bitter is a British style of beer, an ale
X as written at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Rod is sore about a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a man's name made bitter by a kiss; it is a plain rod, and bitter is the beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod on which wheels turn.

clue.text: Conservative centre destroyed: ineffectual chief heads for way out

indicators.note: destroyed means wrecked and broken up, so the letters are rearranged
heads means the first letters of each of the following words

parts.note: their first letters are I and C

explanation.surface: A political sketch: the Tory centre ground is in ruins and its weak leader is heading for the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges C plus CENTRE into ECCENTR; the 'heads' of ineffectual chief add IC. 'way out' is not an exit here but slang for unconventional.
explanation.definitionFit: Way out is informal for highly unconventional or weird, which describes someone eccentric.

clue.text: Wot! Tory right shortly on rampage? Never mind

indicators.note: 'right' is cut down to its abbreviation
the letters go on a rampage and land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the usual abbreviation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Alarm at a right-wing Tory running wild, then a shrug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On rampage' reads as one phrase, but 'on' is two of the letters and only 'rampage' mixes them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are reassurances telling someone not to fret.

clue.text: (& 11ac.) Attempt by his minister to win money from Rishi's doomed venture?

definitions.text: Attempt by his minister to win money
definitions.meaning: people close to the Prime Minister placed bets on the date of the 2024 poll before it was announced
Rishi Sunak's early call of the 2024 general vote, which the Conservatives lost heavily

explanation.surface: A topical jab at the 2024 betting scandal around Rishi Sunak's snap election.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi Sunak was the UK Prime Minister who called a surprise July 2024 election; some of his allies were caught betting on its date. The answer runs on into 11 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling the election early was a gamble, and betting on its date was literally a gamble on the election.

clue.text: see 10ac.
'Inadequate', read by gutted politician

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: to scan a text is to read it

indicators.note: gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the first and last letters

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A devastated Conservative MP reads out a scathing verdict on their performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' strips TORY to its outside letters, TY, which goes 'by' SCAN. 'gutted' looks like the British slang for bitterly disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty means barely enough or insufficient, as in a scanty meal.

clue.text: Player/ambassador with 'City doesn't have it' prognosis

parts.note: a prop is a forward position in rugby
His Excellency, an ambassador's title
CITY without IT

explanation.surface: A footballer and a diplomat forecast that City won't win it.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase looks like a pundit's verdict on a football club; it is an instruction to take IT out of CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophecy is a prediction, a prognosis of what will happen.

clue.text: Touches up in audition break

indicators.note: audition is hearing, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: to paw someone is to touch them up, grope them

explanation.surface: A casting-couch scandal: someone groped during an audition break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' reads as a casting session; here it just means hearing. To touch someone up is British slang for groping them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a brief stop in speech or action is a break.

clue.text: Lack of confidence leads to drugs being taken by Cynthia sadly

indicators.note: being taken by means the drugs go inside the other letters
sadly means in a sorry state, so the letters of the name are muddled

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy, so drugs in the plural are Es

explanation.surface: A woman named Cynthia, losing her nerve, unhappily turns to drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken by' puts the drugs inside the jumbled name, right after its H. E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so Es are drugs; 'leads to' only links definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesitancy is reluctance or indecision, the wavering that comes from a lack of confidence.

clue.text: (& 17ac.) One of 12 celebs swilling gin

parts.note: celebrities are stars

indicators.note: swilling means sloshing about, so the letters of gin are swirled into a new order

explanation.surface: Famous people knock back gin at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One of 12' looks like a reference to 12-across, but the 12 are the signs of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: A star sign is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac in astrology.

clue.text: Get knotted, has-been PM!

definitions.note: read as a command to tie up, as in 'get (it) knotted'
definitions.meaning: knotted means tied up tightly, like a bird bound before roasting
the Conservative Prime Minister of 2022, who lasted just 49 days

explanation.surface: A rude brush-off aimed at a former Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get knotted' is a British way of telling someone to go away; here it is read literally, as tying something up.
explanation.definitionFit: Trussing a chicken or a prisoner means tying it in knots; Liz Truss was a short-lived Prime Minister.

clue.text: Tory leader full of old-fashioned sorrow — not a typical politician's sort of response?

definitions.text: not a typical politician's sort of response?

indicators.note: the leading letter of Tory

parts.note: the first letter of Tory
ruth is an old word for sorrow or pity, so ruthful is full of it

explanation.surface: A Tory leader wallowing in grief gives an answer no politician normally would.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth survives mostly in 'ruthless'; ruthful is its rare opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A truthful answer is, the setter jokes, not what politicians usually give.

clue.text: see 15ac.
Ray's alternative input into alternative energy plants etc

parts.note: the second note of the sol-fa scale is written re or, alternatively, ray
taken as written

explanation.surface: Talk of someone called Ray contributing to green power schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative energy' reads as renewable power, but the second 'alternative' only scrambles.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenery is green plant growth, foliage and the like.

clue.text: Crack cocaine introduced by RAF, true? Rubbish!

indicators.note: cocaine is brought in with RAF and TRUE
the whole lot is rubbished, thrown into disorder

parts.note: the usual abbreviation
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outraged denial that the Royal Air Force brought in crack cocaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like part of 'crack cocaine'; it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in a hairline crack in a bone or a cup.

clue.text: President managed to get round age difficulty?

indicators.note: to get round means to surround, so the ran letters enclose the other piece

parts.note: to run something is to manage it, so managed is ran

indicators.note: age in difficulty is age in trouble, so its letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: An elderly president found a way past worries about his age.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get round' wraps the word for managed around the jumbled age. Ronald Reagan was the oldest US president of his time, so his age was a real campaign issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the 40th President of the United States, from 1981 to 1989.

clue.text: Military's first out-and-out drone

indicators.note: take the first letter of Military

parts.note: the first letter of Military
an out-and-out fool is an utter one

explanation.surface: A military's top-of-the-range drone aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drone' looks like the military aircraft; here it is a verb, to speak in a low monotone.
explanation.definitionFit: To mutter is to speak low and indistinctly, much as a drone is a low monotonous sound.

clue.text: Cyclops Award presented to right dick

parts.note: Cyclops is the setter, who refers to himself
the British honour one rank below the OBE
the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: The setter gives himself an award and hands it to some jerk.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's own name stands for ME. An MBE is a British royal honour. Member and dick are both slang for penis.
explanation.definitionFit: Member is a euphemism for the penis, which dick is slang for.

clue.text: Cordiality, so battle period not on

parts.note: a battle is fighting, war
MONTH without ON

explanation.surface: Friendliness breaks out, so a spell of fighting is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' sounds like a verdict that the battle is off; it tells you to remove ON from the period.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a warm manner is a friendly, cordial one.

clue.text: (& 5dn.) "Move over!"– US parent going round Korea rudely

indicators.note: going round means the parent's letters surround the other piece

parts.note: mom is the American spelling of mum

indicators.note: rudely means roughly, so the letters of Korea are treated roughly and scrambled

explanation.surface: An American mother barges around Korea, shouting at people to shift.
explanation.walkthrough: The parent is the American mom, not the British mum, which the clue's 'US' signals; 'going round' splits it either side of the scrambled country.
explanation.definitionFit: Make room is said to someone to ask them to shift aside, just as move over is.

clue.text: Like the sadistic sex worker, refrain from draping drippy man around one

indicators.note: DON'T is draped round the rest

parts.note: to refrain from something is to not do it: don't!

indicators.note: the man goes around the one
drippy means wet and wishy-washy, so the letters lose their shape

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A dominatrix reins in her urge to wrap herself round a feeble client.
explanation.walkthrough: A dominatrix is the dominant partner in sadomasochistic play, hence the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominatrix plays the dominant role.

clue.text: Study like crazy to dispense with second job

indicators.note: the letters go crazy and swap places
the second letter, S, is dropped

parts.note: STUDY with its second letter, S, dispensed with

explanation.surface: Advice to cram furiously so you can skip a second job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second job' reads as moonlighting; 'second' actually picks the letter to throw out.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the tasks you are obliged to do make up your job.

clue.text: Miss sporting result, being dull

parts.note: to miss something is to lack it

indicators.note: sporting means wearing or showing off, here taken as a playful rearranging of the letters

explanation.surface: Losing a match leaves the team flat and listless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sporting' looks like part of a match report, but it is the anagram signal; 'being' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacklustre means lacking energy or brilliance, so flat and uninspiring.

clue.text: Long period, drug-free: end of addiction? Don't swallow it!

indicators.note: free means without, so the drug letter is taken out

parts.note: a year is a long period of time
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of addiction

parts.note: the final letter of addiction

explanation.surface: An addict celebrates a long time off drugs, at the end of the habit; a warning not to swallow anything follows.
explanation.walkthrough: In 'drug-free', E is ecstasy and 'free' removes it. 'swallow' sounds like taking pills, but here it means believe: a yarn is a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarn is a long, often far-fetched story, the kind of tale a listener should not swallow, meaning believe.
